facts.t: Appears in 0.09% of the 42,331 paintings in our archive (38 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 21).
In our 42,331-painting archive it is rarer than 69% of the named colors.
Peaks in the 1800s: found in 0.0% of the 13,828 paintings we have from then (5 paintings). Against the same museums' baseline that is 0.7x the expected rate.
Inside a painting it most often plays a light (62% of the 21 paintings, by lightness rank within each painting, so varnish cannot fake it).

First seen in our archive in 1437 (commons-Q18685978, by Hans Multscher); the third-earliest painting is 1452, and the latest 2000 (24 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. That is 518 years before the name's earliest record in our sources (1955): the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment or dye.
In printed English the word peaks in the 1940s and rose fastest in the 1990s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
